issues.summary: [PROJECT-GUIDE] Agent execution contract, readiness gate and delivery order
issues.outcome: A versioned Jira catalog prevents generic or incomplete tickets from being dispatched and synchronizes managed Jira fields without rewriting completed history or workflow state.
issues.context: The v1.2 catalog covered every issue but generated broad acceptance text and synthetic permissions. Catalog v1.3 makes semantic readiness enforceable, shards specifications by epic, and adds canary-only synchronization plus an explicit promotion gate.
inScope: Compile all v1.3 epic shards into one deterministic 401-record catalog and reject duplicate Source-IDs or Jira keys.
Reject executable leaves that lack concrete repository paths, artifacts, authorization actions, AC-to-test mapping, reproducible commands, or refined parents.
Synchronize descriptions, labels, Module, parents, issue types, and typed dependency links with backup, optimistic concurrency, canary limits, and no implicit creation or workflow transition.
outOfScope: Unlisted provider credentials and production policy values.
Direct cross-service database reads or duplicated ownership.
Unreviewed workflow transitions, historical rewrites, or destructive migration shortcuts.
businessRules: A decision is publishable only after named owner approval, effective time, supersession rule, fixtures, and rollback impact are recorded.
Example values are DRAFT/UAT only unless an explicit production policy is maker-checker approved.

contracts.name: Atlassian Jira Cloud REST API v3
contracts.compatibility: Use Source-ID and Jira key identity, preserve comments, worklogs, attachments, sprint and status, and abort on concurrent updated timestamps.

contracts.name: ViStay Jira catalog v1.3 JSON schema
contracts.compatibility: v1.2 stays immutable; v1.3 is compiled from per-epic shards and validated before synchronization.

interfaces: Version GraphQL/gRPC/Kafka/OpenAPI contracts before consumer implementation; document owner, caller, schema version, timeout, and compatibility.
Callable HTTP/GraphQL workflows include success, authorization-negative, validation, conflict, replay, and dependency-failure Postman examples.
Events use transactional outbox/inbox, stable aggregate identity, event ID, occurred-at time, producer schema version, and replay-safe consumers.
dataOwnership: Versioned policy and decision records are owned by platform_contracts; runtime services consume published versions and never silently invent defaults.
stateMachine: Specification moves from needs-refinement or decision-required to executable only after semantic validation; executable leaves become agent-ready or agent-ready-after-dependencies from live dependency state.
Jira workflow transitions are never performed by catalog synchronization; Ready promotion and Backlog demotion use the separate promotion gate.
Completed Jira issues are historical and their descriptions remain immutable; remediation is represented by a new Bug or Tech Debt issue.

dataPartitions: PROJECT:SCRUM only; credentials must have explicit project permission and may not enumerate other Jira projects.
fieldGroups: DELIVERY_SPEC is managed from the catalog; WORKFLOW_EVIDENCE, COMMENTS, ATTACHMENTS, WORKLOGS, SPRINT and STATUS remain Jira-owned.

failureSemantics: Return stable validation, forbidden, not-found, conflict, stale-revision, dependency-unavailable, and rate-limit codes without leaking PII.
Fail closed when authorization, authoritative projection, policy version, or required dependency is unavailable.
Retry only transient operations with bounded exponential backoff; route exhausted asynchronous work to a visible repair queue.
idempotencyConcurrency: Every externally retried mutation requires a scoped idempotency key, canonical request fingerprint, durable result, and mismatch rejection.
Use expected revision or equivalent compare-and-swap; concurrent winners are deterministic and losers receive conflict with current revision.
Consumers deduplicate by event ID and business key and support replay without duplicating money, inventory, notification, or audit effects.

acceptanceCriteria.given: the 26 v1.3 source shards containing all managed project issues
acceptanceCriteria.when: npm run validate:jira is executed in platform_contracts
acceptanceCriteria.then: one deterministic 401-record catalog is built, all Jira keys are present, and structural plus semantic validation succeeds

acceptanceCriteria.given: an open issue still contains generator boilerplate or lacks a concrete path, artifact, authorization action, AC mapping, or command
acceptanceCriteria.when: that issue is marked executable or dispatchable
acceptanceCriteria.then: validation fails and the issue cannot receive agent-ready

acceptanceCriteria.given: a reviewed catalog and a fresh Jira backup
acceptanceCriteria.when: a canary Apply is requested for at most five Source-IDs
acceptanceCriteria.then: only those issues are updated, any concurrent Jira edit aborts the run, no workflow status changes, and a repeated selected DryRun reports zero changes

tests: Catalog build and semantic validation cover identity, hierarchy, readiness, repository, authorization, acceptance, test-command, and evidence invariants.
Jira Validate and DryRun cover credential access, catalog-to-live identity, Module options, typed links, managed-field drift, backup, and reviewable plan generation.
Canary Apply plus selected zero-diff DryRun proves idempotent synchronization without touching Jira-owned workflow evidence.

testCases.evidence: platform_contracts console output showing 401 valid records, readiness counts, zero unsafe dispatchable records, and zero missing Jira keys
timestamped Jira backup and JSON dry-run plan for SCRUM-537
Apply result followed by a selected DryRun with changes=0 and unchanged Jira workflow status

observability: Propagate trace and correlation IDs across GraphQL/gRPC/Kafka/webhook boundaries without logging secrets or protected fields.
Emit transition, latency, error-code, replay/deduplication, dependency, and repair-queue metrics with bounded-cardinality labels.
Provide dashboard/alert thresholds and a runbook for stuck states, reconciliation mismatch, and rollback.
definitionOfDone: Catalog validation and all affected repository CI checks pass.
Contracts, migrations, compatibility path, implementation, Admin Web/Mobile parity where applicable, and Postman/Newman evidence are merged.
Security-negative, concurrency/replay, observability, reconciliation, and rollback evidence is linked in Jira.
No production secret or unapproved monetary/policy default is committed; ServiceOwner acceptance evidence is attached before Done.
evidence: Pull request and commit links per repository.
Automated test and Newman report with fixture version.
Migration/rollback or compatibility evidence where data/contracts change.
Dashboard, trace, audit, and reconciliation screenshots or machine-readable artifacts.
issues.decisionNoteVi: Các quy tắc nghiệp vụ và ranh giới dữ liệu trong catalog v1.2 đã được chốt; thay đổi sau này phải tạo phiên bản policy/contract mới, không sửa ngược lịch sử.
